ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184, administered by FINTRAC; Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 114.1–114.3 (register of individuals with significant control – ISCs) and s 118.1 (records); Alberta Corporations Transparency Act, SA 2021, c C-29.5 (public beneficial-ownership registry, not fully proclaimed as of this Stage 1 assessment); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, s 21.1 (federal ISC register, as amended by SC 2023, c 26 and SC 2023, c 32); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), SC 2017, c 21; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss 462.3, 462.31; Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27; College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants Act, SC 2019, c 29, s 292.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all incorporators, directors, ISCs, and key clients/foreign counterparties against (i) United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, (ii) Canadian autonomous sanctions schedules under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA) and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), (iii) FINTRAC published guidance on Politically Exposed Persons and Heads of International Organizations (PEPs/HIOs) including domestic and foreign PEPs, and (iv) where applicable, OFAC SDN lists and EU/UK consolidated sanctions for cross-border payment routing through US and EU correspondent banking systems. Enhanced due diligence is mandated for PEPs/HIOs, for clients using trust or offshore structures, and for fund flows from high-risk FATF-designated jurisdictions; all screening results must be documented in the corporate AML risk assessment and escalated to FINTRAC as suspicious transaction reports where legally required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES system) accessed through authorized Alberta Registry Agents using the national NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system; federal parallel: Corporations Canada online portal (https://ised-isde.canada.ca/corporations) if federal CBCA incorporation is elected
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must contain only Latin characters (English and/or French alphabet); Alberta does not mandate transliteration into any local script. The name must include a mandatory legal element (Limited, Ltd., Incorporated, Inc., Corporation, Corp., or French equivalents) and may not contain punctuation other than periods, commas, ampersands, or dashes. An extra-provincial or foreign corporation may register its existing name in romanized form with a distinctive Alberta element.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Trustco, Loan, Insurance, Assurance (financial services terms requiring federal or provincial licensing)
University, College, Institute (in an educational context) – restricted under the Post-secondary Learning Act, SA 2003, c P-19.5, requiring ministerial consent
Immigration Consultant, Citizenship Consultant, Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) – restricted use absent active licence from the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants
Lawyer, Barrister, Solicitor, Notary, Legal – reserved for licensed legal professionals
Engineer, Engineering, Professional Engineer – reserved under the Engineering and Geoscience Professions Act, SA 2000, c E-11

Royal, Government, Police, RCMP, United Nations, Olympic, Cooperative, Credit Union – suggestive of state, royal, charitable, or regulatory endorsement and require ministerial or other lawful authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS name search report is valid for 90 days from issuance; a one-time extension of up to 90 days may be secured through the registry agent before the original expiry if the report is linked to a pending incorporation. If the Registrar rejects the proposed name or later directs a change of name under ss. 11–12 of the Alberta Business Corporations Act, the incorporator may: (i) file a Name Search Reconsideration / Statement of Objection with the Alberta Corporate Registry within 90 days of the refusal or directive; (ii) submit documentary evidence of consent from the holder of a confusingly similar name or trademark, or demonstrate lawful entitlement to the restricted token; (iii) apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review of the Registrar's decision under s. 12 ABCA and the Administrative Procedures and Jurisdiction Act, RSA 2000, c A-3; and (iv) in parallel, obtain a fresh NUANS report and re-file with a revised distinctive element.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable – the ABCA (ss. 101 and 128) requires a registered office and a records address within Alberta with a physical street address; a P.O. Box is prohibited. A virtual or agent-provided registered office is permissible provided it is staffed during normal business hours, accepts service of process, and forwards mail promptly. This is standard market practice for study-abroad and immigration advisory corporations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – general corporate enforcement: less than 5% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Alberta Corporate Registry. Elevated risk channel: if the corporation engages in regulated immigration consulting, the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC) conducts proactive practice inspections under the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants Act (typically 1–3% of licensees per year). Additional FINTRAC examination risk applies if the firm registers as a money services business (MSB) for escrow and wire-transfer payment rails; FINTRAC MSB examinations are generally triggered by desk-based compliance assessment, with on-site inspection reserved for non-responsive or suspect entities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, sections 4, 15, 17, 22-24, and 101 (registered office and records)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1 under the Alberta Business Corporations Act)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; a zero nominal capital structure is permitted. No escrow account for paid-up capital is required at formation, but all immigration/study-abroad client funds must be held in a CICC-compliant client trust/escrow account prior to any service delivery.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation and Articles of Incorporation of the Corporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act are approved and the issued common shares under the share subscription list are hereby ratified. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the registered office is established at the complete address stated in the Articles, and that the registered office records shall be maintained at that address as required by the Act. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the following persons are appointed to the offices set out opposite their names to serve as directors and officers, authorized to execute and file all applications and documentation, open banking and escrow accounts, and incur obligations necessary for commencement of business activities until otherwise determined by the Board. All acts previously taken by the sole incorporator in connection with formation are approved and ratified in all respects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via Corporate Registry Online (Service Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request through the Corporate Registry Online portal or an authorized service provider; select up to three proposed distinctive names; verify no confusingly similar existing corporate names exist within Alberta and federally; obtain the Name Search Report and reserve the approved name for up to 90 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusing similarity, submit a revised name request citing differences in legal element and dominant distinctive word; a new NUANS report may be required and the reservation date re-starts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Authentication of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / legal officer or authorized incorporation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, setting the corporate name, registered office address, share structure, compliance with the Act's restrictions, and any unanimous shareholder agreement references. Ensure each incorporator executes the Articles and witnesses sign where applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registry flags incomplete data, revise the Articles, resubmit through the online portal, and pay any corrected filing fee; the incorporation is deemed filed as of the original submission date if corrected within the prescribed statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and Obtaining Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Articles of Incorporation with the Corporate Registry online or in person, pay the statutory filing fee via credit card, debit or registered pre-authorized account, and receive the Certificate of Incorporation. Verify the registered office address and legal names precisely as they will appear on the public record.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a filing irregularity is discovered, respond to the Registry's written requisition, file corrected Articles or supplementary forms, and satisfy any additional fee; the Registry issues the Certificate upon full compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, By-Law Adoption and Officer Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a statutory first board meeting; adopt corporate by-laws, approve share subscription and issuance, designate the registered office and records custodian, appoint officers, adopt the corporate seal, and authorize the opening of operational and escrow bank accounts. All actions must be recorded in board minutes and signed.
required_dossiers: Share subscription list and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office address or officer designations are invalid at the registry, file a Notice of Change of Registered Office or Notice of Directors with the Alberta Corporate Registry within the statutory period to cure the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank and Escrow Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian chartered bank or authorized financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Incorporation, board resolution, and identification for Know-Your-Customer review to the financial institution. Open a general operating account and a separate CICC-compliant client trust/escrow account, with dual authorization controls required for disbursement.
required_dossiers: Directors' and officers' passports or government identification
Beneficial ownership and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further information, provide enhanced due diligence documents including corporate records, ownership structure, and intended transaction volume; if refused, apply to another Schedule I bank or invoke the Financial Consumer Agency review complaint procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, Alberta municipal authorities, Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit separate applications for the Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) licence with the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants, municipal business licence with the local city or municipal government, GST/HST and corporate tax registration with the Canada Revenue Agency, and, if applicable, worker compensation and employment registration with the Alberta Workers' Compensation Board.
required_dossiers: RCIC licence application and credential assessment
CRA GST/HST and corporate income tax registrations
Officer identification and conflict of interest declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CICC raises code-of-conduct or sponsorship concerns, respond in writing, provide corrective policies and training certificates, and appear before the licensing committee. If a municipal licence is denied, appeal to the municipal licensing appeals committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC) / Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) Licence and Alberta Municipal Business Licence for International Student Placement and Visa Advisory Services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas / Canadian Environmental Protection Agency (federal for cross-border matters)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Schedule 3 service activity; no full EIA required for a professional office-based study abroad and immigration advisory operation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or point-source emissions are generated; office wastewater must discharge to municipal sewer under the Alberta Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act limits; commercial waste and confidential records must be disposed through licensed waste haulers and secure shredding, with any volatile organic compounds from cleaning/sanitizing products maintained under applicable occupational exposure limits

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the local fire department under the Alberta Fire Code; building occupancy clearance under the Alberta Building Code confirming structural load and occupant capacity; Occupational Health and Safety compliance with the Alberta OHS Act including first-aid equipment, workplace harassment policy, and emergency evacuation plan

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — Business Registration Online (BRO) portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-registration-online.html) and CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services/business-account.html). Alberta corporate income tax is administered and collected by the CRA under the Alberta Corporate Income Tax Act via the single federal T2 return; Alberta's Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA) handles provincial programs. Alberta has no provincial sales tax, so no PST/HST registration is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the Canadian subsidiary under the Canada Business Corporations Act (Corporations Canada) or Alberta Business Corporations Act (Alberta Corporate Registry), obtaining the corporate access number. 2) Register for the 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) with program accounts RC (corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST) and RP (payroll) via BRO, by telephone (1-800-959-5525), or by mailing Form RC1; the BN is the functional TIN/VAT ID. 3) Provide a Canadian address and appoint a Canadian-resident agent for service before the BN is activated. 4) Elect a fiscal year-end (first period cannot exceed 53 weeks) and register for CRA direct deposit to receive GST/HST input tax refunds. 5) Include the BN plus RT0001 program suffix on all GST/HST invoices. 6) File an annual T2 corporate return even for nil amounts; non-resident shareholders need no Canadian TIN for entity operation. Online BN issuance is immediate; RC1 processing takes 10–15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Alberta-incorporated subsidiary is resident in Canada by incorporation (ITA s. 250(4)) and taxed on worldwide income (ITA s. 2(1)). It is a non-CCPC (foreign parent control) and therefore ineligible for the small-business deduction; combined general rate 15% federal + 8% Alberta = 23%. Foreign-source income is subject to foreign tax credits; dividends to the foreign parent are subject to Part XIII 25% withholding, treaty-reduced to 5% at ≥10% voting ownership (15% otherwise) under most OECD treaties. Territorial scope: worldwide taxation for residents; no tax-exempt-zone regime applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election; all corporations are entity-level taxpayers. Available elections: (i) GST/HST closely-related corporation election (ETA ss. 150/156; Form GST25) to treat inter-affiliate taxable supplies as nil-consideration; (ii) functional-currency election (ITA s. 261; Form RC4596) to compute Canadian tax in USD; (iii) non-resident branch election (ITA s. 219) if the foreign parent operates through a Canadian permanent establishment instead of the subsidiary; (iv) hybrid-mismatch relief elections under ITA ss. 18.2(3)/18.2(4) (deduction/non-inclusion relief after a 12-month inclusion window) and ITA s. 18.21 for imported mismatches; (v) the s. 216 net-rental election is available only for real-property rental income and is irrelevant to fee-for-service income. CCPC small-business-limit allocations (ITA s. 256) are unavailable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST), Part IX of the Excise Tax Act, administered by the CRA. Alberta applies only the federal 5% GST; there is no HST or provincial sales tax component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold — registration becomes mandatory at the end of the quarter in which the registrant's (plus associated persons') worldwide taxable supplies in the four preceding calendar quarters exceed CAD 30,000 (ETA ss. 148, 240, 156.1). Both taxable and zero-rated study-abroad/immigration-consulting fees count toward the threshold. Voluntary early registration is advisable to recover input tax credits on Canadian inputs. Because the subsidiary carries on business in Alberta, reverse-charge rules (ETA ss. 217.1/218.01) apply only to unregistered non-resident suppliers, not to this entity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, or digital stamping is in force in Canada. Mandates: (1) GST/HST returns must be e-filed via GST/HST NETFILE where annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 1,500,000 (ETA s. 273.1); (2) books and records must be retained for six years (ETA s. 286); (3) every taxable/zero-rated invoice over CAD 30 must show the BN (RT account), date, recipient, description, consideration, and rate/tax (ETA ss. 169, 223); simplified invoices allowed under CAD 150. The Pan-Canadian Peppol 'PINT Canada' e-invoicing standard is voluntary as of 2026; no CRA API clearance or stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating (0% GST) applies to services supplied to a non-resident recipient (ETA Sch. VI, Part V, s. 7(1)) unless the service is rendered to an individual present in Canada at the time of supply, or relates to real property or tangible goods situated in Canada. Study-abroad placement and immigration/visa consultancy to a client physically outside Canada qualifies: a visa/study-permit application is a personal right, not an interest in Canadian real property or goods, consistent with CRA technical bulletin B-080 and settled interpretive practice. Services to a client already in Canada (e.g., in-Canada study-permit extension) are taxable at 5%. The registrant must retain contemporaneous proof of the client's non-resident location and must bifurcate mixed Canadian/international fees on invoices under a written allocation; otherwise the entire fee is taxable at 5%. Full input tax credits are available for GST paid on inputs attributable to zero-rated exports.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Customs Export Declaration (Form B13/B13A) — only if physical promotional materials ship abroad; for pure consultancy, the signed engagement agreement is the operative export document
Bill of Lading / airway bill — only for accompanying physical shipments; otherwise the scope-of-work and service-milestone records

Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 wire confirmation — evidencing FX payment from the non-resident client's foreign bank account into the Canadian corporate account for each zero-rated invoice
Non-resident status certification — Form RC-3 or notarized attestation confirming foreign residency and presence outside Canada at each service milestone

Visa/immigration file records — study-permit or visa applications, consular receipts and embassy correspondence evidencing the service was performed for Canadian immigration purposes and not in relation to Canadian real property or situated goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits zero-rating claims through GST/HST risk analytics and cross-border financial data (CRS/FATCA and SWIFT payment traces). Where 0% is wrongly applied, the CRA reassesses the full consideration at 5% GST with compound daily arrears interest at the prescribed quarterly rate plus 4 percentage points for corporations (ETA s. 280.1). Penalties: (1) 5% failure-to-remit penalty plus 1% per full month, up to 12 months (ETA s. 280); (2) 5% accuracy penalty plus 50% gross-negligence penalty on the 'false statement amount' for knowing or grossly negligent misstatements (ETA s. 285.01); (3) criminal prosecution for wilful evasion (ETA s. 327): up to CAD 100,000 fine and/or 5 years' imprisonment on indictment; (4) professional-discipline revocation by the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants. Reassessment windows: 4 years normally, extended to 10 years for misrepresentation/neglect/wilful default (ETA s. 298(4)); the GST/HST general anti-avoidance rule (ETA s. 274) can reopen linked transactions contrived to obtain ITCs or zero-rating benefits. ITCs tied to the mischaracterized supply are clawed back with interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as central monetary authority and fiscal agent; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as prudential regulator of deposit-taking institutions and authorized foreign banks; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as the AML/ATF supervisor and Money Service Business (MSB) registrar; Department of Finance Canada as sanctions, international financial policy, and payments-system authority. Canada operates no dedicated Foreign Exchange Control Administration; exchange matters are managed through the market, prudential bank supervision, and statutory AML reporting rather than through ex-ante FX licensing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada adheres to IMF Article VIII; the Canadian dollar is fully convertible with no exchange-control statute, no capital-account licensing, no restriction on capital repatriation, and no distinction between current-account and capital-account convertibility. Profit-remittance hurdles are tax- and corporate-law centered rather than FX-centered: (i) dividends and interest paid to non-resident shareholders are subject to Part XIII withholding tax of 25% statutory, with treaty-reduced rates applicable (e.g., Canada-China DTA may reduce dividends and interest to 10%; Canada-India DTA may reduce certain dividends to 15%); (ii) the Alberta business corporation must satisfy the solvency test in sections 42-43 of the Alberta Business Corporations Act before any distribution, and must be current on CRA filings and Part XIII return obligations; (iii) funds may be freely wired to any jurisdiction through a bank in Canada, subject only to ordinary CDD/EDD screening, sanctions screening under Canada's Special Economic Measures Act, the Criminal Code, and the United Nations Act, and to FINTRAC reporting thresholds; (iv) for inbound equity subscriptions, corporate records must be updated in the Alberta Corporate Registry, and the bank will require board resolutions and share-register evidence; (v) currency conversion is unrestricted at market rates via any authorized bank, foreign-exchange broker, or registered MSB, provided the underlying transaction documentation is retained for at least five years.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed repatriation timeline. An Alberta corporation may hold export receipts in CAD or foreign currency in any chartered bank or authorized foreign bank branch. Remaining obligations are informational and AML-related only: (i) international electronic funds transfers (EFT) of CAD 10,000 or more are reportable to FINTRAC by the financial institution, and the corporate exporter must supply the underlying commercial documentation upon request; (ii) exports of professional services such as study-abroad placement and immigration-visa consulting are captured by Statistics Canada and the Canada Border Services Agency through balance-of-payments trade-in-services reporting, not by the central bank; (iii) foreign-exchange gains and losses on export proceeds must be tracked for CRA corporate income tax purposes under section 39 of the Income Tax Act; (iv) all foreign-currency transactions remain subject to sanctions screening and the enterprise's own AML/ATF compliance program, including record-keeping of the underlying service contracts and tuition/visa-file evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.banking_aml_risk_tier_assessment: Medium_Risk_Enhanced due to the international-student-placement and immigration-visa advisory model, the prevalence of lump-sum tuition and success-fee deposits, cross-border remitter concentrations, and PEP/golden-visa exposure. Anticipated controls include enhanced due diligence, segregated client trust or escrow accounts, beneficiary and originator screening, source-of-funds documentation at CAD 100,000 or higher thresholds, quarterly compliance reviews, and mandatory licence verification through the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
ATB Financial (Alberta Treasury Branches, a provincial Crown corporation)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium (supplementary rail only; not permissible as the primary escrow depository). Canada does not issue an EMI licence; therefore an offshore digital bank or fintech EMI holding Canadian client funds must either be an authorized foreign bank branch (Schedule III) under the Bank Act or operate as a FINTRAC-registered Money Service Business (MSB) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, with additional obligations under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) supervisory framework phased in by OSFI during 2024-2025. Offshore EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, and Payoneer may serve as secondary collections and supplier-payment rails for EUR, GBP, CNH, INR, and other cross-currency operating flows, but they must not hold client tuition and visa fees in lieu of a chartered-bank client trust escrow. The Alberta entity must itself avoid functioning as an unregistered MSB when transmitting funds on behalf of clients; fee settlement should be structured as principal-to-principal payment for the corporation's own professional services, with escrow balances remaining exclusively at a Canadian Schedule I bank or licensed trust company. Passing client funds through an unregulated offshore EMI is a KYC and regulatory blocker.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FINTRAC regulations under the PCMLTFA permit electronic identity verification and do not statutorily require physical appearance of all directors. In practice, Alberta-based Schedule I banks (RBC, TD, BMO, and to a lesser extent Scotiabank, CIBC) will require, for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced immigration-consulting entity with non-resident ownership, at least one authorized signatory or a designated in-Canada corporate secretary/compliance contact to attend an in-person onboarding interview at a Calgary or Edmonton commercial banking centre, combined with a physical verification of the registered office. Remote video onboarding is accepted only when the entity or its principals already maintain a Canadian personal or commercial banking relationship at the same institution, or when an Alberta-licensed lawyer or notary certifies the identity documents and corporate records. ATB Financial mandates physical attendance of the compliance officer and a director for commercial escrow onboarding. Non-resident directors must provide notarized passport copies, residential address proof, and tax-residency declarations, and must execute a written delegation of authority in favour of the in-Canada signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership concentration: a Canadian corporation with all directors and UBOs resident in China, India, GCC states, or Vietnam, with a first-year forecast transaction volume above CAD 1.5 million and no prior Canadian banking relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Certificate of Incorporation and complete Articles; registered-office lease and Alberta Corporate Registry corporate update confirmation; certified register of directors and shareholdings maintained under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; FINTRAC-compliant beneficial-ownership declaration for every person owning or controlling 25% or more; notarized passports, residential address proof, tax-residency certificates, and source-of-wealth statements for all UBOs; board resolution designating the in-Canada signatories; forecast cash-flow model linked to signed Designated Learning Institution (DLI) agreements and immigration-file pipeline; bank reference letters from the UBOs' home-jurisdiction financial institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing or inactive regulatory licence for immigration and visa consulting: absence of a valid College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC) licence or practising rights under section 91 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, which is a mandatory KYC blocker across all six banks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid CICC licence with the RCIC-IRCC registration number of every advising partner; certificate of authorization or partnership attestation if legal services are rendered, including Law Society of Alberta membership; errors-and-omissions insurance certificate (minimum CAD 1 million per claim); AML compliance program adopted under section 9.6 of the PCMLTFA including policies, procedures, and a designated compliance officer; client engagement agreements complying with CICC Rules; annual CICC continuing-education and compliance-review certificates; MOU or agency agreement with each foreign DLI and each sub-agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow contamination and rapid in-and-out wire chains: commingling of client tuition and visa-success fees with operating revenues, or same-day wires to unrelated trust or shell accounts in Hong Kong, UAE, and Singapore before visa adjudication.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Segregated client trust/escrow ledger at a Schedule I Canadian bank; written escrow agency agreement expressly conditioning disbursement on IRCC visa approval or DLI enrollment confirmation; sample DLI offer letters bearing the IRCC DLI number; IRCC application numbers for all underlying beneficiaries; quarterly escrow reconciliation audited by an independent CPA firm; enforceable refund policy and anti-fraud standard operating procedure; two-person maker-checker wire governance; 30-day transaction-monitoring log evidencing no unduly rapid in-and-out movements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Golden-visa and residence-investment programme exposure: lump-sum wires above CAD 500,000 intended for wealth-based immigration programmes, triggering PEP and high-risk-country indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced PEP and sanctions screening records for every beneficial owner and remitter; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth report for each transaction above CAD 100,000; documentary proof of the underlying lawful immigration or residence programme, such as a provincial nomination certificate from the Alberta Advantage Immigration Program or a Startup Visa letter; trust deed, family-company chart, and notarized declarations where funds are routed through family structures; signed statement that funds are not derived from proceeds of crime; appointment of an AML officer under the PCMLTFA with named escalation authority; financial-intelligence-unit escalation log and commitment to file a suspicious-transaction report to FINTRAC where warranted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions or sanctioned financial institutions: transfers involving Iran, Russia, Belarus, North Korea, Syria, Crimea, or OFAC/UN-listed entities, which cause immediate account freeze if not pre-screened.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed corporate sanctions policy; independent sanctions-screening system covering the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council sanctions, and United Kingdom/EU consolidated lists; due-diligence file on each beneficiary bank; contractual clause requiring counterparties to disclose any sanctions nexus; clean trade-sanctity report for the transaction; established voluntary-disclosure protocol to the bank's sanctions compliance unit where a red flag is identified; five-year record retention for all screening logs.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Canada imposes no exchange-control approval for inbound capital, but routing must satisfy bank CDD, OSFI financial-crime standards, and CRA Part XIII rules. Protocol: (1) instruct the non-resident shareholder or parent to send an SWIFT MT103 from its own bank to the receiving Canadian Schedule I bank's Alberta branch; (2) in the MT103 Field 70, insert an unambiguous narrative purpose, because Canadian banks do not use SAFE-style numeric purpose codes: Share subscription - [corporate legal name] - Alberta Certificate number [number] for equity, or Shareholder loan - loan agreement dated [date] for debt, supplemented by the bank's own Statement of Purpose form; (3) pre-funding, deliver a board resolution authorizing the issuance or borrowing, the signed subscription agreement or shareholder-loan agreement, an updated share register, and, where a treaty-reduced withholding rate is claimed, a treaty-residency certificate from the remitter's competent tax authority; (4) when the aggregate inbound amount exceeds an internal bank threshold (typically CAD 250,000 to CAD 1,000,000), provide source-of-wealth evidence from the remitter's bank and a sworn declaration of lawful funds; (5) after clearing, update the Alberta Corporate Registry records to reflect the new shareholders or debt, and complete any CRA Part XIII filings on future interest or dividend remittances; (6) for shareholder loans, charge a commercial arm's-length interest rate, observe the Canadian thin-capitalization ratio under section 18(4) of the Income Tax Act, and document the notional interest where a zero-coupon structure is used; (7) aggregate inflows must be reconciled monthly against the corporate capital table, and the bank must be able to answer FINTRAC reporting and explain-transaction requests; (8) funds originating from high-risk jurisdictions will be pre-cleared for 24-72 hours until the originator, beneficial owner, and purpose are verified.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Commercial clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 direct corporate-to-beneficiary remittance for tuition payments to foreign DLIs, immigration visa-filing fees, and overseas vendor invoices, each backed by the underlying engagement contract or invoice; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700 and MT707 amendments) for large milestone-based contracts requiring a bank payment undertaking, with the Alberta issuing bank acting under UCP 600 through a beneficiary-country advising bank; (iii) domestic CAD electronic transfers via Payments Canada (Lynx and ACSS) for Alberta and inter-provincial supplier and payroll settlements; (iv) SWIFT MT202 COV for correspondent-funded cover payments where the beneficiary bank is outside direct SWIFT reach; (v) FX spot and forward draws under a board-approved treasury limit for cross-currency disbursements. Compliance overlay: every outbound wire must reference the underlying service contract, DLI enrollment document, or immigration file; payments to foreign agents must be supported by executed agency agreements and Canadian withholding-tax analysis; all cross-border wires at or above CAD 10,000 are captured by the bank's international-EFT reporting; beneficiary-name screening against Canadian autonomous sanctions, OFAC SDN, and UN lists is mandatory; and disbursements from the client trust escrow require the escrow instruction letter and the visa-approval or DLI-enrollment trigger document before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable over-the-counter FX forwards (plain vanilla) in CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/CNH executed with a Schedule I bank or authorized foreign bank branch under a board-approved treasury policy and ISDA-style master agreement; no underlying-trade documentation is required by Canadian law, but bank credit limits and prudent-risk limits apply.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or offshore currencies, specifically offshore Chinese renminbi (CNH) and Indian rupee (INR), to hedge tuition-fee and commission exposures where local deliverability is unavailable; settlement is in CAD or USD against a recognized CNH/INR reference rate.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (dual-currency CCS) to hedge both principal and interest exposure on non-resident shareholder loans and large inbound equity-subscription capital.
Exchange-traded FX futures and FX options listed on the Montreal Exchange (TMX Group) and executed through an IIROC/CIRO-registered investment dealer.

European-style plain-vanilla FX options in the OTC market, purchased to cap adverse rate movements on seasonally scheduled visa-fee and tuition disbursements, documented under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and CSA credit-support annex.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.banking_relationship_governance: The entity must maintain a documented treasury policy approved by its board, name a Canadian-resident treasury officer and compliance officer, execute a bank-agreed delegation of signing authority, implement maker-checker controls for all wires above CAD 50,000, reconcile escrow ledgers monthly, and provide the bank with updated CICC licence status and corporate registry filings on an annual basis.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Business Corporations Act Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary date of incorporation or of the date the corporation came under the ABCA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registrar may issue a default notice and strike off or administratively dissolve the corporation after continued non-filing; reinstatement requires an application, payment of arrears and a corrective annual return.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta provincial corporate tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration through the T2 process
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the taxation year; the net tax balance is generally payable by two months after year-end, with a three-month window for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; late payment interest compounded daily; repeated failure after a demand can increase the penalty to 10%; directors may be personally liable for unremitted source deductions or unpaid corporate tax in limited circumstances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual registered office and director confirmation submitted with the annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with the annual return within the same one-month anniversary window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or inaccurate statutory information renders the annual return defective; continued non-compliance with director and registered office record obligations may trigger a registry compliance audit and administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private Alberta corporation may dispense with an auditor where all shareholders consent annually and the corporation is not a distributing corporation; an audit is compulsory if any shareholder holding at least 5% of voting shares requisitions one, or if the corporation distributes securities to the public.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises; non-public reporting private businesses may adopt Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); financial statements prepared for CRA filing must reconcile with the statutory accounting basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta Business Corporations Act and Canada's significant-control-person regime require the corporation to maintain a register of individuals with significant control and to record any share transfer or ownership change within 15 days of becoming aware. The annual return confirms directors, registered office and share structure; material beneficial-ownership changes do not require a separate UBO filing with the Alberta Corporate Registry but must be reflected in the register and be available for inspection by regulatory authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO register)
Minute Book containing articles, by-laws, resolutions and share records

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction: 11% combined rate on first CAD 500,000 of active business income for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPC); investment tax credits; scientific research and experimental development (SR&ED) credits; Alberta innovation employment grant.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically via CRA e-file or NETFILE (mandatory for most corporations).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income (all sources, including business, property, and capital gains).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents carrying on business in Canada must report Canadian-source income; treaty relief may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (after deductions, loss carryforwards, and exemptions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute taxable income per Part I rules; non-residents may be subject to Part XIV tax on certain income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax payable (before provincial allocation and credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Federal tax applies to Canadian-source business income; provincial allocation may be nil if no permanent establishment.
Alberta tax applies only if the corporation has a permanent establishment in Alberta; otherwise allocate to other provinces.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax payable (federal + provincial, net of credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure all credits (e.g., foreign tax credits) are claimed; non-residents may claim treaty-based reductions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of balance due plus 1% per month up to 12 months; interest on unpaid amounts; additional penalties for repeated failures; potential criminal prosecution for gross negligence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding tax under a tax treaty, the non-resident recipient must provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from their home jurisdiction and submit Form NR301 (or equivalent) to the Canadian payer. The payer must retain the TRC and supporting documentation. For dividends, treaty rates typically range from 5% to 15% depending on shareholding and treaty terms.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 25% for both royalties and interest. Treaty rates: royalties often 10% (or 0% for certain IP), interest often 15% (or 0% for arm's length financial institutions). Reduced rates require TRC and treaty eligibility.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Transactions with non-residents exceeding CAD 1 million (for services) or CAD 5 million (for goods, intangibles, or financing) trigger mandatory Local File and Master File documentation. Smaller transactions may still require contemporaneous documentation if they are not at arm's length.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) but applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and treaty abuse provisions. A corporation must demonstrate real economic activity (e.g., employees, premises, decision-making) to claim treaty benefits and avoid recharacterization of transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false deductions, or deliberate misrepresentation of cross-border transactions to reduce tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act (s. 239): fines up to 200% of the tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years, and full restitution of taxes, interest, and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes (s. 227.1) if they failed to withhold or remit; civil restitution, travel bans, and potential imprisonment for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a corporation with no real business activity, no employees, no physical presence, and solely for tax avoidance or treaty shopping.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may disregard the entity under GAAR, deny treaty benefits, reassess taxes, and impose penalties up to 50% of the tax benefit (s. 163.2).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held jointly and severally liable for penalties and taxes if they knowingly participated in the sham; potential criminal charges for conspiracy.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register as a Money Services Business (MSB) or report suspicious transactions under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), especially when handling client funds for immigration or visa services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1 million for individuals and CAD 2 million for corporations; criminal penalties up to 5 years imprisonment for willful non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal fines and imprisonment if they knowingly fail to implement AML compliance programs; civil liability for damages to clients.
